title: transaction_debugger plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `transaction_debugger` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component TransactionDebuggerConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

SummaryLogSchema.description: Customizable output schema for transaction-log JSON / line protocol. Rename keys, drop fields, reorder, inject static stamping, emit derived fields, flatten metadata. Metadata redaction always applies on every code path — sensitive substrings (`authorization`, `cookie`, `password`, `token`, …) cannot be introduced via `static_fields` or `derived_fields` (rejected at construction). This object, each `derived_fields` entry, and `metadata` are strict fixed shapes: unknown keys are rejected with a nested path. HTTP summaries include the normalized terminal `grpc_status` field (separate from `response_status_code`) when the request is gRPC. It can be renamed, omitted, or ordered like every other native field. `api_chargeback`, `api_chargeback_sink`, and `transaction_debugger` reuse this same shape against their own record families; whatever a family cannot express (`summary_type`, `timestamp_format`, `metadata`, `order`, or a derived kind with no source field) is rejected at construction with a plugin- and field-specific diagnostic. Constraints this document cannot express are still enforced at construction and are NOT relaxations of the runtime contract: `omit` / `rename` / `order` names must resolve against the record family's field inventory for the selected `summary_type`; a field may not be both omitted and renamed; the combined native, static, and derived output keys must be unique; `order` must list every non-extension output key unless it contains `"*"`; and `rename` targets, `static_fields` keys (including nested keys) and `derived_fields` names may not match a sensitive-data substring or a credential-class name (for example `session_id`, `client_assertion`, `gpg_passphrase`, `private_rsa_key`; see docs/log_schema.md), while a `static_fields` string value that looks like a literal HTTP auth credential is refused. Under `metadata.mode: flatten`, `omit` may not list `metadata` and `rename` may not rename it; under `metadata.mode: omit`, `rename` may not rename it (those directives would otherwise be silently ignored). The whole `static_fields` object serialized as JSON (escaped keys and values, quotes, separators, braces) must be at most 16384 bytes and a static value may nest at most 8 objects/arrays deep. `transforms` keys must be fields of the selected `summary_type`, may not also be omitted, `ip_prefix` applies only to `client_ip` / `backend_resolved_ip`, and a `hash` `secret_ref` must resolve to a set `FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>` value of at least 32 bytes. See docs/log_schema.md.

summary_type.description: Which summary type(s) this schema applies to. Summaries of the other type fall back to native serialization (the schema only customizes types it claims to handle).

omit.description: Native field names to drop from output.

rename.description: Map of native field name -> output key (at most 128 bytes).

order.description: Explicit output order, by output key. May contain `"*"` once as a wildcard for "every unlisted entry in natural order." Without `"*"`, every field must be listed. Entries are unique — a repeated output key (or a second `"*"`) is rejected.

static_fields.description: Literal JSON values injected at top level. Keys / nested keys matching sensitive substrings or credential-class names (for example `session_id`) are rejected at compile time. A `null` value is rejected — use `omit` to drop a field. At most 64 entries; keys are at most 128 bytes; the whole object serialized as JSON (escaped keys and values included) is at most 16384 bytes; a value nests at most 8 objects/arrays deep. Static fields are stamped into every record, so these bounds are a per-record cost cap.

derived_fields.description: Computed values; emitted alongside native fields.

name.description: Output key for the derived value.

kind.description: `status_class`: `"1xx"`–`"5xx"` from `response_status_code` (stream: `"none"`). `backend_host`: hostname from `backend_target` (port stripped, IPv6 brackets honored). `summary_kind`: `"http"`, `"stream"`, or `"websocket_disconnect"` (the last only for `ws_logging` WebSocket disconnect entries). `outcome`: `"ok"` / `"error"`.

prefix.description: Prepended to each metadata key when promoted to top-level (e.g. `"meta_"`); only `flatten` reads it. Control characters are rejected. The type and the control-character restriction are validated in every mode, so a `nested` or `omit` schema cannot carry a value that would only start failing once the mode is switched to `flatten`.

on_collision.description: Behavior when a metadata key collides with an already-emitted field; only `flatten` reads it. `skip` keeps the existing value; `overwrite` replaces the colliding field's value in place with the (redacted) metadata value, so every key appears exactly once in the record. Validated in every mode, like `prefix`.

timestamp_format.description: Conversion applied to timestamp string fields (`timestamp_received`, `timestamp_connected`, `timestamp_disconnected`). Parse failures fall back to the raw RFC3339 string.

transforms.description: Per-field value transforms, keyed by native source field name (before `rename`), applied when the field is emitted: `truncate` keeps at most `max_bytes` bytes (cut on a UTF-8 boundary); `ip_prefix` keeps the network prefix of an IP address (`ipv4_bits` default 24, `ipv6_bits` default 48; IPv4-mapped IPv6 is masked as IPv4; a value that is not an address is emitted as `null`); `hash` replaces the value with the lowercase-hex keyed HMAC-SHA-256 under the secret named by `secret_ref`, which must be a `${FERRUM_PLUGIN_SECRET_<NAME>}` reference resolved at construction (literal secrets are refused; the value must be at least 32 bytes). Only the transaction-summary loggers support `transforms`; `api_chargeback`, `api_chargeback_sink`, and `transaction_debugger` reject the key, and statsd ignores it. Kafka partition keys and Loki labels read typed fields and are not transformed.

TransactionDebuggerConfig.description: Plugin: transaction_debugger — Emits verbose request/response and terminal diagnostics via tracing::debug on the transaction_debug target. Requires FERRUM_LOG_LEVEL=debug to see output. Unsupported keys are rejected. Body capture is opt-in and default off. It never forces an ineligible message to buffer: a body is sampled only when the message declares an identity Content-Encoding, a Content-Length that fits inside the configured cap (or, with the explicit capture_body_prefix opt-in, a text/plain or form Content-Length up to 1048576 bytes), and a capturable textual Content-Type (application/json, +json, text/json, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, text/plain). gRPC (application/grpc*), SSE (text/event-stream), WebSocket upgrades (including H2/H3 Extended CONNECT, excluded by typed request provenance rather than headers), XML, GraphQL, multipart, text/html, binary media types, chunked/unknown-length, and encoded messages keep streaming and are reported as omitted with a stable reason. XML and GraphQL are excluded because Ferrum has no bounded structure-aware redactor for them. Request samples are taken after all request transforms (backend-visible bytes) and response samples after all response transforms (client-visible bytes). Content-Length is only an admission screen: both final body hooks re-check the actual body length against the configured cap before any scan and fail closed with a content-free over_capture_limit omission, and an actually empty body (a HEAD or 304 response declares a length it never sends) is reported with the fixed empty_body reason rather than as a malformed structured body. Samples are redacted before rendering (JSON/form per field, text/plain per line as a coarse operator opt-in, plus credential-shaped values anywhere). In text/plain bodies every `name=value` / `name: value` line is dropped unless each field name parses cleanly and is declared in safe_text_fields (fail closed), a malformed JSON body renders as a fixed content-free marker instead of a partial rendering, control and bidi characters are escaped, non-UTF-8 bodies (including an incomplete multibyte tail) render as a fixed marker, and every capture reports whether it was captured, truncated, binary, or omitted. When the transaction_debug DEBUG target is disabled no body is buffered for capture. Captured bytes go only to the transaction_debug tracing target and are never written into transaction-log metadata. Values are also screened by shape regardless of field or header name: compact JWS/JWE tokens (recognized from the base64url-decoded JSON protected header, so whitespace inside the header does not evade it), well-known provider API keys, AWS access key ids, and PEM private-key blocks are redacted in captured bodies and in header dumps. Exactly one capture record is emitted per enabled direction even when a transform flips the decision between the header phase and the final body hook. Capture can be targeted with capture_request_header (plus an optional exact capture_request_header_value), capture_sample_rate, and capture_expires_at; a request outside the target never buffers and is reported as omitted with reason not_selected or capture_expired. capture_body_prefix opts text/plain and form bodies whose declared Content-Length exceeds the cap (up to 1048576 bytes) into buffering and renders a redacted prefix of complete lines or pairs marked truncated; JSON, chunked/unknown-length, and larger bodies are unchanged.

capture_body_prefix.description: Admit text/plain and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies whose declared Content-Length exceeds the capture cap (up to 1048576 bytes) and render a redacted prefix of the complete lines / pairs that fit inside the cap, marked truncated. JSON bodies, which need the whole document for field redaction, and chunked/unknown-length bodies are unchanged. True requires log_request_body or log_response_body true. Null is rejected.

capture_sample_rate.description: Fraction of requests whose bodies are captured, chosen deterministically per request so both directions agree. Requests that are not sampled never buffer and report reason not_selected. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true.

capture_request_header.description: Capture only requests that carry this request header (an HTTP header token, compared case-insensitively). Other requests never buffer and report reason not_selected. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true.

capture_request_header_value.description: Exact value capture_request_header must carry (compared after trimming the received value). 1-256 visible ASCII characters without surrounding spaces. When set, the selector header is redacted from header dumps. Requires capture_request_header.

capture_expires_at.description: RFC 3339 instant after which capture stops: requests received at or after it never buffer and report reason capture_expired. A past instant is accepted. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true.

redacted_headers.description: Additional header names to redact beyond the built-in sensitive list. Each entry must be a nonempty HTTP header token (RFC 9110 tchar). Empty strings and names with spaces are rejected.

log_request_body.description: Enable bounded, redacted capture of the backend-visible request body. Null is rejected.

log_response_body.description: Enable bounded, redacted capture of the client-visible response body. Null is rejected.

max_request_body_bytes.description: Per-request capture budget in bytes. Requires log_request_body true; out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Per-response capture budget in bytes. Requires log_response_body true; out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped.

redacted_body_fields.description: Additional body field names (compared case-insensitively) to redact beyond the built-in credential markers. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed before the 128-character maximum is applied. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true when the array is nonempty. An empty array is valid without a capture switch. Independently of this list, everything under an Azure "On Your Data" `parameters` object inside a `data_sources` / `dataSources` / `data-sources` container is replaced wholesale. Recognizing that container name never short-circuits the ordinary visitor: a captured body is arbitrary JSON, so a value under that name which is not the provider's conventional array (an object, string, number, boolean, or null) is still traversed with the same member-name and credential-shaped-string rules as the rest of the body.

safe_text_fields.description: Field names (compared case-insensitively) whose `name=value` / `name: value` lines may be rendered in captured text/plain bodies. A line containing `=` or `:` is kept only when every delimiter follows a declared name; a line with a missing, empty, quoted, undeclared, or non-ASCII-identifier name is dropped. Entries that the credential classifier or the sensitive body-field rules match are rejected: a credential-shaped name cannot be declared safe. Requires log_request_body or log_response_body true when the array is nonempty.

schema_ref.description: Name of a schema registered by a `transaction_log_schema` plugin. Mutually exclusive with `schema`. Projects the terminal diagnostic records (HTTP, stream, WebSocket disconnect) emitted on the `transaction_debug` target; the diagnostic field inventory is the plugin's own (`outcome`, `method`, `path`, `status`, `rejection_phase`, `latency_plugin_ms`, …), not the transaction summary's. A portable named schema can only reference names shared with the summary registry, so use an inline `schema:` for diagnostic-only fields. See docs/log_schema.md.
